name: menu
title: Menu
lead: Display contextual actions with positioning, auto-close, keyboard navigation, and submenus.

variants.title: Actions and disabled items
variants.description: Static presentation sample: native disabled buttons cannot activate. For unavailable links, remove or guard the destination; CSS disabled styling is not a keyboard guard.
variants.markup: Unavailable destination

variants.title: Headers and descriptions
variants.description: Static content composition with explicit readable foregrounds. Headers and descriptions do not create a command controller.
variants.markup:

Choose how to share.

variants.title: Scrollable menu
variants.description: A real toggle initializes keyboard handling; menu-scrollable constrains overflow using the actual max-height fallback token.

variants.title: Submenu structure
variants.description: Initialize the owning top-level toggle. Nested submenu triggers receive popup/expanded state; logical entry/exit keys follow document direction. This example uses click submenu activation.

variants.title: Auto-close policies
variants.description: Default, inside-only, outside-only and manual policies govern clicks. Escape still closes while focus is in a menu, including autoClose=false; forms are exempt from normal inside-click closing.

variants.title: Responsive placement
variants.description: Placement prefixes use viewport breakpoints. Floating UI resolves logical end from the document direction, flips/shifts when necessary and updates on resize.

variants.title: Native form content
variants.description: Generic menus can contain native forms. Clicking the checkbox keeps the menu open; no application-menu roles or automatic submission behavior are added.

variants.title: Selected and translucent presentation
variants.description: Selected/check styling is authored state, not an automatic radio or selection model. Translucent adds backdrop filtering.

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: Static dark presentation uses logical alignment. Interactive submenu arrow direction follows the document, not only an isolated dir wrapper.

keyboard.behavior: Open from the toggle and focus enabled items; navigation stops at each end once inside.
Focus the first/last enabled item in the current menu.
Enter/leave a submenu; reversed for an RTL document.
Activate a native item or open its submenu.
Close the current submenu or root menu and return focus to its trigger, regardless of autoClose.
Use native focus navigation; eligible menus close when focus leaves. Forms and autoClose policy affect dismissal.

guidelines: Use data-trm-toggle="menu" even with programmatic calls so global keyboard/close handling can find the trigger.
Floating UI is required: use the bundle or resolve the dependency in a module build.
Menu does not add complete ARIA application-menu roles or typeahead. Use native links/buttons and author an appropriate complete widget model if required.
Disabled styling alone does not guard an anchor; use native disabled or remove/guard the destination.
Static show examples illustrate styling; initialized toggles demonstrate the JavaScript contract.
show/hide start events are cancelable on the trigger. shown/hidden report settled CSS transitions; hide restores any moved menu to its original parent.
container can move the menu outside clipping ancestors; test geometry, focus and document RTL. update recalculates placement.

events.hidden.trm.menu: On the toggle after exit and Floating UI cleanup; a moved menu is restored to its original parent.
events.hide.trm.menu: Cancelable start on the toggle; clickEvent is supplied for click-driven dismissal.
events.show.trm.menu: Cancelable start on the toggle, before opening or moving the menu.
events.shown.trm.menu: On the toggle after the entry transition settles, if still open.

keyboard.behavior: Automatically select/focus the next enabled tab in DOM order, wrapping at the end, including RTL.
Select/focus the previous enabled tab, wrapping at the start. Modifier shortcuts are not intercepted.
Enter/leave the tab list through its selected trigger; author panel tabindex when it needs a focus stop.

guidelines: Author IDs, aria-controls, aria-labelledby, initial aria-selected and focusable panels; do not rely on the plugin to invent every relationship.
Use dynamic tablist/tab/tabpanel roles for panel switching, not ordinary page navigation.
Active triggers initialize on window load; newly inserted widgets require explicit initialization.
hide on the old trigger and show on the new trigger are cancelable. hidden notifies immediate outgoing removal; shown waits for the entering pane.
show returns a completion promise; stale pending activations do not emit a misleading shown notification.
Both arrow axes follow DOM order regardless of orientation or RTL; unmodified arrows/Home/End activate automatically.
Do not place tabs in menus: the pinned documentation explicitly warns about usability and accessibility problems.

events.click.trm.tab: Internal namespaced DOM listener; not a dispatched plugin lifecycle event.
events.hidden.trm.tab: On the outgoing trigger after immediate deactivation; relatedTarget is the incoming trigger.
events.hide.trm.tab: Cancelable start on the old trigger; relatedTarget is the incoming trigger.
events.keydown.trm.tab: Internal namespaced DOM listener; not a dispatched plugin lifecycle event.
events.load.trm.tab: Internal namespaced DOM listener; not a dispatched plugin lifecycle event.
events.show.trm.tab: Cancelable start on the incoming trigger; relatedTarget is the old trigger, if any.
events.shown.trm.tab: On the new trigger after the pane entry callback; stale activations are ignored.
